title: Laredo man involved in shooting faces federal charge - NewsBreak
text: A man wanted for shooting at another person is facing federal charges, according to court documents. Jorge Alejandro Diaz was charged with possession of a firearm by a person who has been convicted in any court of a crime punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year. On June 17, the Laredo Police Department Texas Anti-Gang (TAG) Unit along with Laredo Police Special Operations Group, Homeland Security Investigations, U.S. Border Patrol and the Drug Enforcement Administration set up an operation by the 2000 block of Colonia Street. Authorities obtained search and arrest warrants stemming from an investigation into an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon offense where Diaz was the suspect, according to court documents. Investigators set up surveillance in the area and observed Diaz enter a gray Kia Soul. Authorities then pulled over Diaz for a traffic violation and took him into custody for the active arrest warrant, according to an arrest affidavit. Officers, investigators and agents executed a search warrant at a residence in the 2000 block of Colonia Street. The search resulted in the seizure of suspected drugs, over 100 rounds of ammunition and a 9mm Glock 43X handgun. Authorities found the firearm in the master bedroom closet in a man’s jacket, according to the affidavit. Diaz was transported to LPD headquarters. “Diaz agreed to speak to investigators and subsequently admitted to shooting at the victim of the alleged aggravated assault, and that the firearm recovered from his house was the same firearm he used in the shooting,” the affidavit states. “Diaz also admitted that he was a previously convicted felon and that he knew he was prohibited from possessing firearms.” Diaz added that he had the firearm for protection and that he had possessed the gun for about two years, court documents state. A records check on Diaz revealed multiple arrests and convictions, including a felony conviction for possession of a controlled substance in December 2015 and another felony conviction for manufacturing, delivering a controlled substance in September 2015.
